candidates.title: Voice-change triggers for targeted clinical reassessment
candidates.question: Can a sustained within-person shift in home voice features identify when an additional clinician assessment is more informative than waiting for the next scheduled visit?
candidates.new_claim: Input delta: shifts the objective from predicting the interpolated UPDRS value on each recording to deciding when to request a new clinical measurement. It proposes a persistent, person-calibrated voice-change trigger whose value is judged by independently measured subsequent change, not row-level fit.
candidates.domain_value: Could concentrate clinician time on periods when a patient's voice departs persistently from their personal baseline, while avoiding routine alerts for transient variability.
known_basis_refs: Supplied UCI 189 documentation: repeated home voice measurements, 42 people, approximately six months; motor_UPDRS and total_UPDRS are linearly interpolated.
assumptions: A person's voice has a sufficiently stable personal reference distribution over some clinically useful baseline window.
A sustained voice-feature shift can sometimes precede or accompany a clinically meaningful change, but may also reflect non-disease factors.
An alert is useful only if an independent assessment can be obtained within a prespecified interval.
candidates.variables_and_units: Voice features: supplied recording-level measurements (feature-specific units/scales undocumented here); time: days since recruitment (test_time); trigger: standardized within-person multivariate distance or prespecified feature change, dimensionless; outcome: change in clinician-assessed motor UPDRS points between actual visits; decision: alert/no alert per person-week.
candidates.testable_prediction: In a prospective cohort with actual clinician assessments, persistent voice-triggered windows will contain a greater proportion of prespecified clinically meaningful motor-UPDRS changes within the next 14 days than matched non-trigger windows from the same participants, at a fixed alert rate.
candidates.alternative: Voice shifts primarily reflect recording conditions, vocal effort, medication timing, intercurrent illness, or ordinary day-to-day variability and do not enrich for independently assessed clinical change.
candidates.discriminating_test: Freeze the personal baseline, voice features, persistence rule, clinical-change threshold, 14-day horizon, and maximum alert rate before prospective evaluation. Compare triggered windows with within-person non-trigger windows matched on calendar time and assessment opportunity. Primary contrast: proportion with independently assessed clinically meaningful motor-UPDRS change; report sensitivity and alerts per person-month. A prespecified null/equivalence margin distinguishes no useful enrichment from a clinically useful trigger.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Only exploratory construction of candidate personal baselines and trigger definitions, and assessment of how often triggers would fire. Because target scores are interpolated between clinical assessments and raw clinical visit anchors are not supplied, this dataset cannot establish alert enrichment, lead time, or clinical utility.
candidates.required_new_data: Prospective repeated home recordings with timestamps; raw dates and values of actual clinician motor-UPDRS assessments (not interpolated labels); prespecified clinically meaningful change threshold; and contemporaneous medication timing and basic recording-context/illness annotations to interpret false alerts. Unit of evaluation: person-week, with participant-level uncertainty.
candidates.failure_condition: At the prespecified alert burden, triggered windows do not exceed matched non-trigger windows by the minimum clinically useful enrichment, or apparent enrichment disappears after accounting for assessment timing and annotated context.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Do voice-derived longitudinal change or anomaly triggers prompt clinical reassessment using independently observed outcomes, rather than predict interpolated UPDRS scores? Search prior work on personalized voice monitoring, change-point/anomaly detection in Parkinson's speech, and alert-triggered assessment; distinguish trigger utility from prediction accuracy.

candidates.title: Separate disease-related voice change from recording context
candidates.question: How much apparent within-person voice change under home monitoring is attributable to recording context or vocal state rather than change in clinically assessed motor function?
candidates.new_claim: Input delta: turns a prediction task into a measurement-validity study that estimates whether standardized repeated voice tasks and lightweight context annotations reduce within-person disagreement with actual clinical change.
candidates.domain_value: Could identify which low-burden protocol or annotations are needed before voice trends are used for remote monitoring decisions.
known_basis_refs: Supplied UCI 189 documentation: recordings were automatically captured at home; targets are interpolated clinical scores.
assumptions: Recording context and vocal state vary over time and are not fully represented by the supplied acoustic variables.
A short standardized task plus context annotation can reduce some measurement variation without removing clinically relevant signal.
candidates.variables_and_units: Within-person voice-feature change per recording (feature units as recorded); standardized-task indicator and annotations for medication timing, illness, and recording context; actual motor-UPDRS point change between clinical visits; paired within-person comparison of protocol conditions.
candidates.testable_prediction: For paired recordings collected under usual home conditions and a standardized task within the same day, standardized-task features with context annotations will show lower within-person test-retest dispersion and stronger agreement in direction with independently assessed between-visit motor-UPDRS change than unannotated usual-condition features.
candidates.alternative: Standardization does not improve reliability or agreement, or removes useful variation; apparent disagreement is mainly because voice and motor UPDRS measure different constructs.
candidates.discriminating_test: Collect both recording conditions on the same days, repeat each condition, record context/medication timing, and obtain actual clinical assessments. Predefine a feature summary and compare within-person repeat dispersion and directional agreement with subsequent actual UPDRS change; include a no-context-adjustment comparator.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: No: the supplied fields do not include repeated paired protocol conditions, context annotations, or actual visit-level target anchors. Existing rows may support only exploratory assessment of feature repeatability across time, which cannot identify the proposed context effect.
candidates.required_new_data: Same-day repeated usual-condition and standardized-task voice recordings, recording-context and medication/illness annotations, exact visit dates, and actual clinician motor-UPDRS scores. Unit: paired recording day nested within participant.
candidates.failure_condition: Standardized and annotated recordings do not reduce prespecified within-person dispersion or improve directional agreement beyond uncertainty, or improvement is not reproducible across participants.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Which standardized speech tasks and context covariates improve within-person longitudinal reliability and agreement with actual Parkinson's clinical assessments in home voice monitoring?

candidates.title: Choose a voice sampling cadence by change-detection value
candidates.question: At what home-recording cadence can a voice-monitoring system detect a sustained personal deviation with acceptable delay and burden, when clinical assessments occur much less often?
candidates.new_claim: Input delta: treats sampling frequency as an operational design variable and evaluates detection delay and recording burden against prespecified sustained voice shifts, instead of optimizing a row-level regression metric.
candidates.domain_value: Could reduce unnecessary recording burden while preserving timely detection of persistent changes that warrant review.
known_basis_refs: Supplied UCI 189 documentation: roughly 200 recordings per participant over about six months, with repeated recordings and interpolated clinical targets.
assumptions: The observed schedule contains enough temporal coverage to simulate less frequent sampling of voice-feature deviations, though not to establish disease-change detection.
A persistent voice deviation is a candidate operational signal, not a validated surrogate for clinical progression.
candidates.variables_and_units: Sampling cadence: recordings per week; detection delay: days from onset of a prespecified sustained feature deviation to trigger; burden: recordings per person-month; outcome for future validation: actual clinician UPDRS change in points.
candidates.testable_prediction: When the same prespecified persistent-deviation rule is applied to subsampled schedules, a moderate cadence will achieve a lower recording burden than daily sampling while keeping median detection delay below a predefined operational limit; this is a design prediction about voice deviations only, not clinical deterioration.
candidates.alternative: Sparse sampling misses or delays many deviations, or observed deviations are too unstable for cadence optimization to be meaningful.
candidates.discriminating_test: Using fixed person-level time series and a fixed deviation rule, replay several prespecified sampling cadences with repeated random phase offsets. Compare detection delay and recordings per person-month; freeze an operational delay limit and select the lowest burden cadence meeting it. Then validate that cadence prospectively against actual assessment changes.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Partly: recording times and voice measures permit an exploratory replay of detection of voice-feature deviations, but variable observation schedules and the absence of independent clinical event times preclude conclusions about clinical detection or optimal deployment cadence.
candidates.required_new_data: Prospective recordings at randomized or assigned cadences, actual clinical assessment dates and scores, and adherence/burden measures; ideally multiple participants with different disease trajectories. Unit: participant trajectory, with cadence assignment at participant or participant-period level.
candidates.failure_condition: No tested lower-burden cadence meets the frozen delay limit reliably across participants, or the cadence that detects voice deviations does not detect independently assessed clinical changes.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: How has sampling cadence been selected for longitudinal digital biomarkers or Parkinson's voice monitoring using detection delay, measurement burden, and independently observed clinical events?

sources.title: Dam safety assessment through data-level anomaly detection and information fusion
sources.original_abstract: The anomaly detection and safety assessment of dams have attracted increasing attentions. To assess the safety of dams, a novel dam safety assessment model is proposed. The safety assessment model consists of data-level anomaly detection and information fusion. In the anomaly detection, a novel model based on the generative adversarial network and variational autoencoder is proposed. Through the stepwise training, the anomaly scores with reconstruction and discrimination losses can be obtained. Considering the multi-source and complexity of information system, a two-step fusion model is proposed. In the multi-source and multi-attribute fusion, the neighborhood rough set model is employed to construct the neighborhood granular structure. Through the idea of granular computing, the uncertainty of these sources and attributes is measured. Then the Sup-Inf fusion functions and fusion weights are employed to integrate the information. Finally, the anomaly scores with interval form are obtained. For verification, an arch dam is taken as an example. Through the analysis of detection and fusion results, the proposed model can detect the abnormal signals accurately and have the comprehensive assessment of the dam.

sources.title: A Hybrid Multi-Model Framework for Personalized User-Level Anomaly Detection With Data-Driven Threshold Optimization
sources.original_abstract: Modern user authentication systems increasingly need user and device behavior aware adaptive mechanism to detect evolving threats beyond the traditional authentication framework of static credential verification. This paper proposes a hybrid multi-model framework for personalized user-level anomaly detection using a data-driven Hybrid Anomaly Score (HAS). Unlike static thresholding approaches, The proposed framework derives algorithm that integrates multiple anomaly detection methodologies to compute HAS through adaptive per-user thresholds (using cohort maturity and percentile-based optimization). The framework is evaluated on 72 million real-world data set. The framework demonstrate 96% precision, 92% recall, and an F1-score of 0.94, while maintaining inference latency within 2-3 ms per authentication event. The ablation analysis of the framework confirms the contribution of dynamic weighting and personalized threshold optimization to improved detection stability and convergence. The proposed framework outperforms existing approaches in both scalability and latency satisfying real-time operational constraint. The results indicate that data-driven adaptive thresholding combined with hybrid anomaly modeling provides an effective and deployable solution for large-scale authentication environments.
